title: Red-Teaming Large Language Models in Low-Resource African Languages: A Case Study of Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin
abstract: arXiv:2610.39590v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become more widespread in Africa, their safety in low-resource languages remains largely untested since most red-teaming work focuses on English. This study evaluates six state-of-the-art LLMs using 400 explicit adversarial prompts in Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin, categorised into four harm categories. The responses were scored by native-speaker annotators and reliability was assessed using Cohen's $\kappa$. While models that rejected up to 69% of English prompts rejected as few as 0% in Yoruba, this was not because they were safer, but because they failed to understand the prompts. Attack success rates increased for most models in the Nigerian languages, with GPT-4o Mini demonstrating the most significant cross-lingual safety discrepancy (+0.23 in Yoruba). translated_title: 在低资源非洲语言中对大型语言模型进行红队测试：以约鲁巴语和尼日利亚皮钦语为例
translated_abstract: 随着大型语言模型（LLM）在非洲日益普及，其在低资源语言中的安全性在很大程度上仍未经过测试，因为大多数红队测试工作都集中在英语上。本研究使用400个明确的对抗性提示词评估了六个最先进的LLM，这些提示词以约鲁巴语和尼日利亚皮钦语编写，并被划分为四个伤害类别。模型响应由母语标注者进行评分，并使用Cohen的κ系数评估评分的可靠性。尽管这些模型拒绝了高达69%的英语提示词，但在约鲁巴语中拒绝率却低至0%，这并不是因为它们更安全，而是因为它们无法理解这些提示词。对于大多数模型而言，在尼日利亚语言中的攻击成功率均有所上升，其中GPT-4o Mini表现出最显著的跨语言安全差异（约鲁巴语中+0.23）。当模型确实对对抗性提示词做出回应时，许多回应是有害的，有害内容的比例在英语中达到0.63，在（原文此处截断）
tldr: 本研究首次针对六个主流大语言模型，使用约鲁巴语和尼日利亚皮钦语的对抗性提示词开展红队安全测试，发现模型在低资源非洲语言中的安全防线明显失效，攻击成功率显著上升，而这主要源于模型对这些语言的理解不足而非更安全的行为。
en_tdlr: This study red-teams six state-of-the-art LLMs using adversarial prompts in Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin, revealing that models are significantly more vulnerable in low-resource African languages—mainly because they fail to understand the prompts rather than being safer—highlighting a critical cross-lingual safety gap.
